programme.subtitle: Auditing, S3 Data Events, Log File Validation & Security Alarms
programme.description: Deploy a multi-Region AWS CloudTrail trail with SSE-KMS encryption, private S3 logging bucket policy, CloudWatch Logs delivery, S3 object data events, digest log file validation, CloudWatch security alarms, and SNS email alerts.
programme.learningOutcome: Master CloudTrail management and data event logging, log file integrity validation, CloudWatch integration, security event monitoring, and governance concepts for the AWS SAA-C03 exam.

phases.title: Phase 1: Administrator Bootstrap, Narrow IAM Policy & Learner Setup
phases.description: Bootstrap training user fa-cloudtrail-user with dedicated policy fa-cloudtrail-training-policy, configure AWS CLI, and explore Event History.

phases.title: Phase 2: Multi-Region Trail, KMS Encryption, Private S3 Bucket & CloudWatch Logs
phases.description: Create KMS key, dedicated private S3 logging bucket, CloudWatch log group, IAM role, and deploy multi-Region trail fa-cloudtrail-trail.

phases.title: Phase 3: S3 Data Events, Activity Generation & CloudWatch Logs Insights Search
phases.description: Configure advanced event selectors for test bucket, generate S3 activity, and search data events via CloudWatch Logs Insights and raw S3 log files.

phases.title: Phase 4: S3 Digest Validation, Security Metric Filter, SNS & Alarm Verification
phases.description: Validate log file integrity via CLI, create CloudWatch metric filter and SNS alarm, and trigger a safe AccessDenied test event.

phases.title: Phase 5: CloudTrail Insights, Lake & SAA-C03 Architecture Comparisons
phases.description: Understand CloudTrail Insights, CloudTrail Lake, KMS requirements, and compare CloudTrail with other AWS monitoring services for SAA-C03.

phases.title: Phase 6: Reverse-Dependency Infrastructure Teardown
phases.description: Clean up all lab resources in strict reverse dependency order, switch to administrator identity for IAM teardown, and remove local CLI profile section.

tasks.title: Administrator Bootstrap, IAM Training User & AWS CLI Setup
tasks.goal: Bootstrap a dedicated training IAM user fa-cloudtrail-user with customer policy fa-cloudtrail-training-policy, configure AWS CLI profile fa-cloudtrail, verify identity, and explore CloudTrail Event History.
tasks.whyItMatters: Using the AWS root account for daily tasks introduces significant security risks. Creating dedicated IAM credentials with least-privilege policies ensures safe hands-on learning and aligns with SAA-C03 security best practices.

consoleSteps.title: Sign in with administrator credentials and open IAM
consoleSteps.instruction: Open the AWS Management Console in your web browser and sign in using your administrator-capable IAM user or role (never the AWS root account).

instructions.text: Open the AWS Management Console in your web browser and sign in using your administrator-capable IAM user or role (never the AWS root account).
In the top search bar, type IAM and select IAM under Services.
In the left navigation menu, click Policies, then click Create policy.
Click the JSON tab, replace the default content with the provided fa-cloudtrail-training-policy JSON block, and click Next.
On the Policy details page, set Policy name to fa-cloudtrail-training-policy and click Create policy.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The customer-managed policy fa-cloudtrail-training-policy is created.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not attach AdministratorAccess to the training user.

consoleSteps.title: Create training user fa-cloudtrail-user and generate access key
consoleSteps.instruction: In the IAM left navigation menu, click Users, then click Create user.

instructions.text: In the IAM left navigation menu, click Users, then click Create user.
Enter fa-cloudtrail-user for User name, leave AWS Management Console access unchecked, and click Next.
Select Attach policies directly, search for fa-cloudtrail-training-policy, check the checkbox next to it, and click Next.
Click Create user.
Click on fa-cloudtrail-user, select the Security credentials tab, scroll down to Access keys, and click Create access key.
Select Command Line Interface (CLI), check the acknowledgment checkbox, click Next, then click Create access key.
Copy the Access key ID and Secret access key safely (you will use them to configure your local AWS CLI profile).

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The IAM user fa-cloudtrail-user is created with fa-cloudtrail-training-policy attached and credentials generated.
consoleSteps.warning: Keep secret access keys safe and never share or publish them in code repositories.

consoleSteps.title: Explore CloudTrail Event History in the AWS Console
consoleSteps.instruction: In the AWS Console top search bar, type CloudTrail and select CloudTrail under Services.

instructions.text: In the AWS Console top search bar, type CloudTrail and select CloudTrail under Services.
In the CloudTrail left navigation menu, click Event history.
Review the event list showing recent management events across your AWS account.
Click on any recent event (such as CreateUser or LookupEvents) to inspect the JSON payload.
Observe key management event fields: eventSource, eventName, userIdentity, sourceIPAddress, resources, requestParameters, and responseElements.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: CloudTrail Event History is displayed and event attributes are verified.
consoleSteps.warning: Event History shows management events from the last 90 days only. It does not record S3 object data events.

cliSteps.explanation: Configures a local AWS CLI profile named fa-cloudtrail. When prompted, enter your Access Key ID, Secret Access Key, Default region name (eu-west-2), and Default output format (json).
cliSteps.expectedResult: Local CLI profile fa-cloudtrail is created and stored in ~/.aws/credentials and ~/.aws/config.
cliSteps.warning: Do not use your root account access keys.

cliSteps.explanation: Verifies that the fa-cloudtrail CLI profile is active and bound to fa-cloudtrail-user.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Returns JSON showing your AWS Account ID and Arn arn:aws:iam::[ACCOUNT_ID]:user/fa-cloudtrail-user.
cliSteps.warning: Record your 12-digit AWS Account ID from the output; you will use it as [ACCOUNT_ID] in subsequent commands.

cliSteps.explanation: Queries the 90-day CloudTrail Event History for recent management events in eu-west-2.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Returns a JSON list of recent management events with EventId, EventName, EventTime, and EventSource.
cliSteps.warning: Data events (such as S3 object puts/gets) are not returned by lookup-events.

verification.title: Verify IAM User Identity
verification.instruction: Run aws sts get-caller-identity --profile fa-cloudtrail in your terminal.
verification.expectedResult: Output shows UserId, Account, and Arn ending with /fa-cloudtrail-user.

verification.title: Verify CloudTrail Event History Console Access
verification.instruction: In CloudTrail Console > Event history, check that management events are visible.
verification.expectedResult: Event history table displays recent API calls with user identity details.

cleanup.title: Task 1 Setup Note
cleanup.instruction: User credentials and policy created in Task 1 will be cleaned up during final Phase 6 teardown.
cleanup.description: User credentials and policy created in Task 1 will be cleaned up during final Phase 6 teardown.
cleanup.verification: No task-level cleanup required during Task 1.

tasks.title: KMS CMK & Dedicated Private S3 Log Bucket Creation
tasks.goal: Create a customer-managed KMS key fa-cloudtrail-key with key alias alias/fa-cloudtrail-key, a private S3 logging bucket fa-cloudtrail-logs-[ACCOUNT_ID], attach the complete CloudTrail S3 bucket policy with source ARN conditions, and enable log file validation.
tasks.whyItMatters: CloudTrail requires specific S3 bucket permissions to deliver log files. Using a dedicated private bucket with SSE-KMS encryption and log file validation ensures audit logs are securely stored and cryptographically protected against tampering.

consoleSteps.title: Create Customer Managed KMS Key fa-cloudtrail-key
consoleSteps.instruction: In the AWS Console top search bar, type KMS and select Key Management Service under Services.

instructions.text: In the AWS Console top search bar, type KMS and select Key Management Service under Services.
In the left menu, click Customer managed keys, then click Create key.
Select Symmetric key type and KMS key usage as Encrypt and decrypt, then click Next.
Set Alias to fa-cloudtrail-key and Description to KMS key for CloudTrail log encryption, then click Next.
Under Key administrative permissions, select fa-cloudtrail-user, then click Next.
Under Key usage permissions, select fa-cloudtrail-user, then click Next.
In the Key policy code editor, ensure cloudtrail.amazonaws.com is allowed to describe keys and generate data keys, then click Finish.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: KMS key fa-cloudtrail-key is created with alias alias/fa-cloudtrail-key.
consoleSteps.warning: Record the KMS Key ID and ARN for trail configuration.

consoleSteps.title: Create private S3 log bucket fa-cloudtrail-logs-[ACCOUNT_ID] and attach bucket policy
consoleSteps.instruction: In the top search bar, type S3 and select S3 under Services.

instructions.text: In the top search bar, type S3 and select S3 under Services.
Click Create bucket.
Enter Bucket name as fa-cloudtrail-logs-[ACCOUNT_ID] (replace [ACCOUNT_ID] with your 12-digit account ID) and select AWS Region eu-west-2.
Ensure Block all public access remains checked (Block Public Access enabled).
Leave default encryption enabled and click Create bucket.
Click on the new bucket fa-cloudtrail-logs-[ACCOUNT_ID], select the Permissions tab, scroll down to Bucket policy, and click Edit.
Paste the complete S3 bucket policy JSON below, replacing [ACCOUNT_ID] with your account ID, and click Save changes.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Private S3 bucket fa-cloudtrail-logs-[ACCOUNT_ID] is created with public access blocked and CloudTrail delivery bucket policy attached.
consoleSteps.warning: The bucket policy must include aws:SourceArn and s3:x-amz-acl = bucket-owner-full-control conditions.

cliSteps.command: aws kms create-key --description "KMS key for CloudTrail log encryption" --profile fa-cloudtrail --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Creates a Customer Managed KMS Key in eu-west-2 for SSE-KMS CloudTrail log file encryption.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Returns JSON containing KeyMetadata with KeyId and Arn.
cliSteps.warning: Record the KeyId and Arn from the output.

cliSteps.command: aws kms create-alias --alias-name alias/fa-cloudtrail-key --target-key-id [KMS_KEY_ID] --profile fa-cloudtrail --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Creates the key alias alias/fa-cloudtrail-key pointing to your new KMS key ID.
cliSteps.expectedResult: KMS key alias is created successfully with no output.
cliSteps.warning: Replace [KMS_KEY_ID] with your actual KMS KeyId.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api create-bucket --bucket fa-cloudtrail-logs-[ACCOUNT_ID] --region eu-west-2 --create-bucket-configuration LocationConstraint=eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudtrail
cliSteps.explanation: Creates private S3 bucket fa-cloudtrail-logs-[ACCOUNT_ID] in eu-west-2 for storing CloudTrail logs and digests.
cliSteps.warning: Replace [ACCOUNT_ID] with your 12-digit AWS account ID.

cliSteps.explanation: Enforces Block Public Access on the S3 logging bucket to prevent public exposure.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Public access block configuration is applied with no error.
cliSteps.warning: Always keep public access blocked for security log buckets.

cliSteps.explanation: Applies the CloudTrail S3 bucket policy stored in fa-cloudtrail-s3-bucket-policy.json to the log bucket.

verification.title: Verify KMS Key Alias
verification.instruction: Run aws kms list-aliases --profile fa-cloudtrail --region eu-west-2 and check for alias/fa-cloudtrail-key.
verification.expectedResult: Output lists alias/fa-cloudtrail-key associated with your KMS key ID.

verification.title: Verify S3 Bucket Policy
verification.instruction: In S3 Console > fa-cloudtrail-logs-[ACCOUNT_ID] > Permissions, inspect Bucket policy.
verification.expectedResult: Policy contains AWSCloudTrailAclCheck and AWSCloudTrailWrite statements with aws:SourceArn.

cleanup.title: Task 2 Resources Note
cleanup.instruction: S3 logging bucket and KMS key will be removed during final Phase 6 reverse teardown.
cleanup.description: S3 logging bucket and KMS key will be removed during final Phase 6 reverse teardown.
cleanup.verification: No task-level cleanup required during Task 2.

tasks.title: CloudWatch Logs Log Group & Multi-Region Trail Deployment
tasks.goal: Create CloudWatch log group /aws/cloudtrail/fa-cloudtrail-logs with 14-day retention, create IAM role fa-cloudtrail-cw-role, and deploy multi-Region trail fa-cloudtrail-trail with SSE-KMS encryption and Log File Validation enabled.
tasks.whyItMatters: Delivering CloudTrail events to CloudWatch Logs enables real-time security alerting via metric filters and alarms. Enabling multi-Region logging ensures global visibility into API actions across all AWS regions.

consoleSteps.title: Create CloudWatch log group and set 14-day retention
consoleSteps.instruction: In the AWS Console top search bar, type CloudWatch and select CloudWatch under Services.

instructions.text: In the AWS Console top search bar, type CloudWatch and select CloudWatch under Services.
In the left menu under Logs, click Log groups.
Click Create log group.
Enter Log group name as /aws/cloudtrail/fa-cloudtrail-logs.
Set Retention setting to 14 days (2 weeks) and click Create.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Log group /aws/cloudtrail/fa-cloudtrail-logs is created with 14-day retention.
consoleSteps.warning: Setting a retention policy prevents indefinite log storage charges.

consoleSteps.title: Create IAM Role fa-cloudtrail-cw-role for CloudWatch Logs delivery
consoleSteps.instruction: In the AWS Console, open IAM > Roles, and click Create role.

instructions.text: In the AWS Console, open IAM > Roles, and click Create role.
Select Custom trust policy.
Paste the trust policy JSON below allowing cloudtrail.amazonaws.com to assume the role, and click Next.
Under Add permissions, click Create policy to open a new tab.
Paste the permissions policy JSON below allowing logs:CreateLogStream and logs:PutLogEvents on /aws/cloudtrail/fa-cloudtrail-logs, name the policy fa-cloudtrail-cw-policy, and click Create policy.
Return to the Create role tab, refresh policies, select fa-cloudtrail-cw-policy, and click Next.
Set Role name to fa-cloudtrail-cw-role and click Create role.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: IAM role fa-cloudtrail-cw-role is created with CloudTrail trust relationship and CloudWatch Logs stream permissions.
consoleSteps.warning: Record the Role ARN arn:aws:iam::[ACCOUNT_ID]:role/fa-cloudtrail-cw-role.

consoleSteps.title: Create multi-Region trail fa-cloudtrail-trail in CloudTrail Console
consoleSteps.instruction: In the AWS Console, open CloudTrail > Trails, and click Create trail.

instructions.text: In the AWS Console, open CloudTrail > Trails, and click Create trail.
Enter Trail name as fa-cloudtrail-trail.
Select Apply trail to all regions (Multi-Region trail).
Under Storage location, select Use existing S3 bucket, and enter fa-cloudtrail-logs-[ACCOUNT_ID].
Check Enable log file validation.
Under Additional settings, check Customer managed KMS key, select Existing KMS key alias/fa-cloudtrail-key.
Under CloudWatch Logs, check Enabled.
Select Existing log group /aws/cloudtrail/fa-cloudtrail-logs and Existing IAM role fa-cloudtrail-cw-role.
Click Next, leave Management events set to Read and Write, click Next, then click Create trail.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Multi-Region trail fa-cloudtrail-trail is active and delivering encrypted logs to S3 and CloudWatch Logs.
consoleSteps.warning: Verify status shows Logging enabled.

cliSteps.explanation: Creates CloudWatch log group /aws/cloudtrail/fa-cloudtrail-logs for real-time CloudTrail event stream.
Sets 14-day retention policy on the CloudWatch log group to control storage costs.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Retention policy updated with no error.
cliSteps.warning: Log retention defaults to Never Expire if not configured.

cliSteps.explanation: Creates IAM role fa-cloudtrail-cw-role allowing CloudTrail to assume the role.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Returns JSON showing created role metadata and Arn.
cliSteps.warning: Ensure fa-cloudtrail-cw-role-trust-policy.json is in the current directory.

cliSteps.command: aws iam put-role-policy --role-name fa-cloudtrail-cw-role --policy-name fa-cloudtrail-cw-policy --policy-document file://fa-cloudtrail-cw-role-permissions-policy.json --profile fa-cloudtrail
cliSteps.explanation: Attaches inline permissions policy allowing logs:CreateLogStream and logs:PutLogEvents on the log group.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudtrail create-trail --name fa-cloudtrail-trail --s3-bucket-name fa-cloudtrail-logs-[ACCOUNT_ID] --include-global-service-events --is-multi-region-trail --enable-log-file-validation --kms-key-id alias/fa-cloudtrail-key --cloud-watch-logs-log-group-arn arn:aws:logs:eu-west-2:[ACCOUNT_ID]:log-group:/aws/cloudtrail/fa-cloudtrail-logs:* --cloud-watch-logs-role-arn arn:aws:iam::[ACCOUNT_ID]:role/fa-cloudtrail-cw-role --profile fa-cloudtrail --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Deploys multi-Region CloudTrail trail fa-cloudtrail-trail with KMS encryption, log validation, S3 delivery, and CloudWatch Logs integration.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Returns JSON detailing trail configuration, TrailARN, and KMSKeyId.
cliSteps.warning: Replace [ACCOUNT_ID] in all ARNs with your 12-digit account ID.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudtrail start-logging --name fa-cloudtrail-trail --profile fa-cloudtrail --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Starts event logging on fa-cloudtrail-trail.

verification.title: Verify Trail Logging Status
verification.instruction: Run aws cloudtrail get-trail-status --name fa-cloudtrail-trail --profile fa-cloudtrail --region eu-west-2.
verification.expectedResult: IsLogging is true, LatestDeliveryTime is populated, and LatestNotificationAttemptSucceeded is true.

verification.title: Verify CloudWatch Logs Group
verification.instruction: In CloudWatch Console > Log groups, select /aws/cloudtrail/fa-cloudtrail-logs.
verification.expectedResult: Log streams are being created with names matching [ACCOUNT_ID]_CloudTrail_eu-west-2.

cleanup.title: Task 3 Resources Note
cleanup.instruction: Trail, CloudWatch log group, and IAM role will be removed during final Phase 6 reverse teardown.
cleanup.description: Trail, CloudWatch log group, and IAM role will be removed during final Phase 6 reverse teardown.
cleanup.verification: No task-level cleanup required during Task 3.

tasks.title: Advanced Data-Event Selectors & Data Event Analysis
tasks.feature: CloudTrail Advanced Event Selectors & CloudWatch Logs Insights
tasks.goal: Create test bucket fa-cloudtrail-test-[ACCOUNT_ID], upload test object sample.txt, configure an advanced event selector on fa-cloudtrail-trail for S3 object data events using StartsWith operator, generate S3 operations, and search data events in CloudWatch Logs Insights.
tasks.whyItMatters: Data events record resource operations (e.g. S3 GetObject, PutObject). Because CloudTrail Event History does not show data events, learners must know how to use advanced event selectors and query data events via CloudWatch Logs Insights or S3 log files.

consoleSteps.title: Create test S3 bucket fa-cloudtrail-test-[ACCOUNT_ID] and upload sample.txt
consoleSteps.instruction: In the AWS Console, open S3, and click Create bucket.

instructions.text: In the AWS Console, open S3, and click Create bucket.
Enter Bucket name as fa-cloudtrail-test-[ACCOUNT_ID] in region eu-west-2.
Keep Block all public access checked and click Create bucket.
Click on fa-cloudtrail-test-[ACCOUNT_ID], click Upload, select a local text file named sample.txt containing Hello CloudTrail, and click Upload.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Test bucket fa-cloudtrail-test-[ACCOUNT_ID] is created and test object sample.txt is uploaded.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not upload real passwords or credentials.

consoleSteps.title: Configure Advanced Event Selector for S3 Object Data Events in CloudTrail Console
consoleSteps.instruction: In the AWS Console, open CloudTrail > Trails, and click fa-cloudtrail-trail.

instructions.text: In the AWS Console, open CloudTrail > Trails, and click fa-cloudtrail-trail.
Scroll down to Data events and click Edit.
Click Add data event type, select S3.
Select Switch to advanced event selectors.
Configure Field selector 1: eventCategory equals Data.
Configure Field selector 2: resources.type equals AWS::S3::Object.
Configure Field selector 3: resources.ARN StartsWith arn:aws:s3:::fa-cloudtrail-test-[ACCOUNT_ID]/.
Omit readOnly so that both read and write operations are captured.
Click Save changes.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Advanced event selector is attached to fa-cloudtrail-trail, scoping S3 object data events to fa-cloudtrail-test-[ACCOUNT_ID]/.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not use readWriteType; readWriteType belongs to basic event selectors. Omitting readOnly captures both read and write operations.

consoleSteps.title: Search S3 Data Events in CloudWatch Logs Insights
consoleSteps.instruction: In the AWS Console, open CloudWatch > Logs > Logs Insights.

instructions.text: In the AWS Console, open CloudWatch > Logs > Logs Insights.
In the Select log group(s) dropdown, select /aws/cloudtrail/fa-cloudtrail-logs.
In the query editor, paste the query: fields @timestamp, eventName, eventSource, responseElements.x-amz-request-id | filter eventSource = "s3.amazonaws.com" | sort @timestamp desc | limit 20.
Click Run query.
Inspect returned logs for PutObject and GetObject data events corresponding to sample.txt.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Logs Insights query returns S3 data event logs showing PutObject and GetObject operations.
consoleSteps.warning: CloudTrail Event History does not return data events. Always use CloudWatch Logs Insights or S3 log files for data event analysis.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api create-bucket --bucket fa-cloudtrail-test-[ACCOUNT_ID] --region eu-west-2 --create-bucket-configuration LocationConstraint=eu-west-2 --profile fa-cloudtrail
cliSteps.explanation: Creates harmless test bucket fa-cloudtrail-test-[ACCOUNT_ID] in eu-west-2 for generating S3 object data events.
Uploads local file sample.txt to the test S3 bucket, triggering a PutObject data event.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudtrail put-event-selectors --trail-name fa-cloudtrail-trail --advanced-event-selectors file://fa-cloudtrail-advanced-event-selectors.json --profile fa-cloudtrail --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Attaches the advanced event selector JSON using StartsWith operator to fa-cloudtrail-trail to capture S3 object data events.
Downloads sample.txt from the test S3 bucket, triggering a GetObject data event.
cliSteps.warning: This generates a GetObject data event captured by the trail.

cliSteps.command: aws logs start-query --log-group-name /aws/cloudtrail/fa-cloudtrail-logs --start-time $(date -d "15 minutes ago" +%s) --end-time $(date +%s) --query-string "fields @timestamp, eventName, eventSource, requestParameters.key | filter eventSource='s3.amazonaws.com'" --profile fa-cloudtrail --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Executes a CloudWatch Logs Insights query searching for S3 data events in /aws/cloudtrail/fa-cloudtrail-logs.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Returns queryId string for checking results with aws logs get-query-results.
cliSteps.warning: Use get-query-results with the returned queryId to view results.

verification.title: Verify Advanced Event Selectors
verification.instruction: Run aws cloudtrail get-event-selectors --trail-name fa-cloudtrail-trail --profile fa-cloudtrail --region eu-west-2.
verification.expectedResult: Output shows AdvancedEventSelectors with eventCategory Data and resources.ARN StartsWith arn:aws:s3:::fa-cloudtrail-test-[ACCOUNT_ID]/.

verification.title: Verify S3 Data Event Logging in CloudWatch Logs Insights
verification.instruction: In CloudWatch > Logs Insights, query for eventSource = "s3.amazonaws.com".
verification.expectedResult: Query results show PutObject and GetObject records for sample.txt.

cleanup.instruction: Test S3 bucket and object will be removed during final Phase 6 reverse teardown.
cleanup.description: Test S3 bucket and object will be removed during final Phase 6 reverse teardown.
cleanup.verification: No task-level cleanup required during Task 4.

tasks.title: CLI Log Validation, Security Alarms & SNS Notification Verification
tasks.goal: Validate log integrity using aws cloudtrail validate-logs, create CloudWatch metric filter fa-cloudtrail-unauthorized-filter, create SNS topic fa-cloudtrail-alerts-topic with email subscription, create alarm fa-cloudtrail-unauthorized-api-alarm, and trigger a safe AccessDenied test event with aws iam list-users.
tasks.whyItMatters: Digest validation uses cryptographic signatures to prove audit logs have not been altered or deleted. Automated security alarms notify security teams immediately when unauthorized API calls occur.

consoleSteps.title: Create CloudWatch Metric Filter for unauthorized API calls
consoleSteps.instruction: In the AWS Console, open CloudWatch > Log groups, and select /aws/cloudtrail/fa-cloudtrail-logs.

instructions.text: In the AWS Console, open CloudWatch > Log groups, and select /aws/cloudtrail/fa-cloudtrail-logs.
Click the Metric filters tab, then click Create metric filter.
In Filter pattern, paste: { ($.errorCode = "*UnauthorizedOperation") || ($.errorCode = "AccessDenied*") }.
Click Next.
Enter Filter name as fa-cloudtrail-unauthorized-filter.
Under Metric details, select Metric namespace as CloudTrailSecurity, set Metric name to UnauthorizedApiCallCount, set Metric value to 1, and click Next.
Click Create metric filter.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Metric filter fa-cloudtrail-unauthorized-filter is created on /aws/cloudtrail/fa-cloudtrail-logs.
consoleSteps.warning: Ensure the pattern matches both UnauthorizedOperation and AccessDenied.

consoleSteps.title: Create SNS Topic fa-cloudtrail-alerts-topic and confirm email subscription
consoleSteps.instruction: In the AWS Console, search for SNS and select Simple Notification Service under Services.

instructions.text: In the AWS Console, search for SNS and select Simple Notification Service under Services.
Click Topics, then click Create topic.
Select Standard, enter Name as fa-cloudtrail-alerts-topic, and click Create topic.
In the topic page, click Create subscription.
Select Protocol as Email, enter your valid email address in Endpoint, and click Create subscription.
Check your email inbox, open the confirmation email from AWS Notifications, and click Confirm subscription.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: SNS topic fa-cloudtrail-alerts-topic is created and subscription status changes to Confirmed.
consoleSteps.warning: You must click the email confirmation link before alarms can send emails.

consoleSteps.title: Create CloudWatch Alarm fa-cloudtrail-unauthorized-api-alarm
consoleSteps.instruction: In the AWS Console, open CloudWatch > Alarms, and click Create alarm.

instructions.text: In the AWS Console, open CloudWatch > Alarms, and click Create alarm.
Click Select metric, browse to CloudTrailSecurity > Metric name UnauthorizedApiCallCount, select it, and click Select metric.
Set Statistic to Sum, Period to 5 minutes, Threshold type to Static, Whenever UnauthorizedApiCallCount is Greater/Equal to 1, then click Next.
Under Notification, select In alarm, choose Select an existing SNS topic, select fa-cloudtrail-alerts-topic, and click Next.
Enter Alarm name as fa-cloudtrail-unauthorized-api-alarm, click Next, then click Create alarm.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: CloudWatch alarm fa-cloudtrail-unauthorized-api-alarm is created and armed.
consoleSteps.warning: Initial state will show OK or INSUFFICIENT_DATA until metrics arrive.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudtrail validate-logs --trail-arn arn:aws:cloudtrail:eu-west-2:[ACCOUNT_ID]:trail/fa-cloudtrail-trail --start-time $(date -d "1 hour ago" +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ") --profile fa-cloudtrail --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Cryptographically validates CloudTrail log integrity against digest files in S3 delivered by fa-cloudtrail-trail.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Returns Output: Results for logs... 0 log files invalid, 0 log files missing.
cliSteps.warning: Digest files must exist in S3 for validation to succeed. Digests are delivered every 1 hour.

tasks.feature: AWS CloudTrail Governance & SAA-C03 Exam Architecture
tasks.goal: Understand CloudTrail Insights, CloudTrail Lake, KMS encryption requirements, and master comparative architectural trade-offs between CloudTrail, CloudWatch, AWS Config, EventBridge, VPC Flow Logs, and AWS X-Ray for the SAA-C03 exam.
tasks.whyItMatters: SAA-C03 exam questions test your ability to select the correct governance or observability tool based on scenario requirements (API auditing vs metrics vs configuration compliance vs tracing).

consoleSteps.title: Review CloudTrail Insights and CloudTrail Lake in the Console
consoleSteps.instruction: In the AWS Console, open CloudTrail.

instructions.text: In the AWS Console, open CloudTrail.
In the left menu, click Insights. Learn that Insights analyzes management events using machine learning to detect unusual operational activity or API call volume spikes.
In the left menu, click Lake. Learn that CloudTrail Lake provides an immutable, managed SQL data lake to query management and data events using SQL syntax across multiple accounts.
Do not enable Insights or create a Lake event data store (both incur additional chargeable fees).

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Insights and Lake concepts are reviewed without enabling chargeable resources.
consoleSteps.warning: CloudTrail Insights and Lake incur additional usage charges.

consoleSteps.title: Compare SAA-C03 Observability & Security Services
consoleSteps.instruction: Review the service matrix below to understand key SAA-C03 distinctions:

instructions.text: Review the service matrix below to understand key SAA-C03 distinctions:
1. AWS CloudTrail: Records WHO called WHAT API, WHEN, and from WHERE (API auditing, governance, compliance).
2. Amazon CloudWatch: Collects metrics, logs, and performance data; triggers alarms and auto-scaling.
3. AWS Config: Tracks resource configuration history, relationship changes, and compliance drift (WHAT is configured).
4. Amazon EventBridge: Event bus for routing events and triggering automated workflows (e.g. EC2 state change to Lambda).
5. VPC Flow Logs: Captures IP network traffic metadata (accepted/rejected packets) on ENIs and subnets.
6. AWS X-Ray: Traces distributed requests through microservice architectures for latency analysis.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Service comparative concepts for SAA-C03 exam scenarios are understood.
consoleSteps.warning: For exam questions: CloudTrail = API call history; Config = resource configuration compliance; CloudWatch = operational metrics/logs.
